reason: 'suborbicular' means about orbicular, so orbicular with the qualifier 'approximately' is right for the stipules. The rare spathulate form is a separate alternative.
'pinkish' means about pink, said of the bracts.

target: position: per margin, in the distalmost 1 cm of the blade
fix: In 'each margin with N teeth on proximal 1/2 and M teeth in distalmost cm', each count is per margin and covers only the stated stretch of margin. Keep 'each margin' and 'distalmost cm' (or 'proximal 1/2') as a count position. Do not record the number as the count of teeth on the whole blade.
reason: 3–6 teeth is the number in the last centimetre of one margin. As a count of teeth on the leaf blade it is false, because the blade has far more teeth.

target: calyculus of the capitulum involucre (outer involucral bracts); not PO epicalyx
fix: In Asteraceae, 'calicule'/'calyculus' means the small outer bracts at the base of the involucre of a flower head, not an epicalyx outside the calyx of a single flower. The PO synonym 'calyculus' on epicalyx should not be used when the context is the involucre (involucre, capitule, bractées involucrales).
reason: Here 'sans calicule' is said of the 1-seriate involucre of an Emilia flower head. PO epicalyx is defined as phyllomes immediately outside the calyx, which is a different structure.
Spikelets tawny at maturity, with the stage 'mature' kept. Grounding 'tawny' (a brownish orange) to ISCC-NBS orange follows the colour synonym table, though an earlier review called it a weak fit.
'floating leaves always absent' is the leaf with 'floating' negated, which is what the flora says.

fix: In 'Leaflets 3, the terminal one X, the laterals Y', each shape belongs to one leaflet position. Keep 'terminal' or 'lateral' as a position slot on the leaflet.
reason: The lateral leaflets are obliquely ovate. 'Rounded-rhomboid' is true only of the terminal leaflet, so the annotation is false for leaflets in general.

target: the stalk segment (isthmus) between fruit articles
fix: 'N mm between articles' in a moniliform fruit (a string of articles) measures the stalk segment linking two articles. It is not the length of the fruit, so do not give the measurement to the fruit.
reason: The fruit is a string of 1–4 articles, each 4.5–8.8 mm long. The whole fruit is not 1.1–4.2 mm long.

target: position: upper (above the basal pair) lateral nerves
fix: In 'with the basal lateral nerves ... and the upper lateral nerves N on each side', the count covers only the upper secondary veins. Keep 'upper' as a position, or add the basal pair before giving a total.
reason: The leaf is 3-nerved from the base, so the total number of secondary veins per side is one more than 3–6. The count is right only for the upper nerves.

target: count 4, rare maximum 5; whole: male flower
fix: Read 'N(M)' with no range as usually N, rarely M: put M in the maximum-extreme slot, not as the top of a 4–5 range. The 'Male flowers:' heading should also fill the whole slot.

fix: In 'midrib impressed above, prominent beneath', each side carries its own value. Keep 'beneath' or 'above' as a place on the midrib, otherwise the two values contradict each other.

fix: 'without tufts of hair' means the tuft of hairs (pappus or coma) is absent. It must not become 'glabrous' negated, which reverses the meaning to hairy. In Asteraceae the achene is the fruit, not the seed.
reason: The flora says the achenes have no tuft of hairs. The annotation says the seed is not glabrous, which is the opposite, and it is put on the wrong part.
